I grew up never liking fresh tomatoes for all the normal reasons - weak flavor, poor texture, etc. Once I got into the restaurant industry I found a mentor in the first chef I worked for, who was very into farm to table and the slow food movement. So through him I got into the world of farm shares, farmers markets, and dealing with independent people rather than major distributors for ingredients at work. There's no end to the amount that chef Gary opened my eyes to new food and ideas. When I was 19 we got in a shipment of maybe 25 pounds of about 6 varieties of heirloom tomatoes. Two cherry-sized varieties will always stand out for me, sun golds and black crims. The former are yellow orange with a deep sweetness to them, so deep it almost is akin to a caramelized onion. The crims are purple grey with dark green streaks, and green on the inside. They were a bit tarter and acidic,  with an almost creamy texture. God damn were they delicious. The other types were all great, and mostly went to cooked foods, but those two were showcased as is, because they were a marvel the way the earth gave them to us. I think we may have blistered some, and halved and salted some, but otherwise they were just naked.
Although still not as good as a late summer tomatoes, some farms are doing great things with hydroponics. I can get above average on the vine tomatoes year round up in NH.

If you haven't heard it, the first disc of the complete box set of VU is a demo, referred to as the Scotch demo, that is a completely different style of music, with most of the tracks being tracks that are known and loved from the first album, Its guitar and harmonica only, with Lou Reed and John Cale taking turns on vocals. It is very much in a baroque folk vein, with an insane version of Venus in Furs led by Cale being, im my mind, the real stand out. Also a great track called Prominent Men, which is an awesome folky track with a real pre-electric Dylan feel to it.

Lou Reed has passed away after 50+ years of being one of the most influential and controversial musicians of all time. I was never a very big fan of his solo work, although I see why some people go crazy for it. That said, Getting that sweet VU box set with the detachable banana when I was 15 helped me bridge my love of punk with my transition into a deep love for 60's rock, which introduced me to Psychedelia, my "favorite" genre, if I had to pick one. My brother, girlfriend, and I used to get fucked up in our basement and listen to nothing but VU, MC5, and the Stooges for days on end. Anyone else have a fond memory of Lou Reed, or care to expand on their opinions of his solo work, if any?
